title: Yosef, Son of Kimchit
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Yoma 47a it is related that once Ishmael ben Kimchit, the High Priest, became ritually impure, and Joseph his brother entered and served in his place; and their mother saw two sons serve as High Priest on one day.
He had a brother named Yeshevav. Hyman says that there were six brothers, all of whom served as High Priest.

notes.text: The notice says six brothers, while Yoma47a says Kimchit had seven sons, all of whom served as High Priest. Six may count Yosef’s other brothers, but that harmonization is not imposed on the supplied wording. The numeral remains a source question.

No new primary scalar was supplied for this entry. The earlier Yoma47a seven-sons consultation is inherited, not newly read here. Hyman’s six brothers and Yeshevav remain unchanged. Counting six other brothers is only a possible harmonization, not what the supplied notice explicitly states, and no numeral is repaired. High-priest service and the mother’s two sons in one day are Hyman’s account, not a new chronological identity binding.

Yoma 47a gives two episodes. In the first, Yeshevav serves in Ishmael’s place after Ishmael speaks with an Arab. In the second, Yosef takes his place after Ishmael speaks with an officer. The following baraita says Kimchit had seven sons who all served in the high priesthood. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 1:1 likewise counts seven, while its parallel story names Shimon and his brother Yehudah. Hyman prints “six brothers.” Whether he meant six besides Yosef remains open.
